summary: Feed s065_single is degraded: 76.6% of TCP sessions (105/137) are one-way, IDS requires bidirectional traffic for stateful analysis. All other checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, drops, overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/TAP is forwarding only one direction of traffic - likely only one side of a bidirectional link is tapped, SPAN is configured as tx-only/rx-only, or asymmetric routing is sending return path via different link not aggregated to this IDS port. 105 of 137 sessions show single direction.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP stream reassembly, handshake validation, and signature matching. With 76.6% one-way sessions the IDS cannot track state, will miss exploits that span request/response, fail to detect C2, and generates incomplete flow logs.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions (client->server and server->client) from both sides of the tap/SPAN at the packet broker and deliver as single bidirectional feed to IDS port so TCP sessions are complete for stateful detection.
